1.text: Tha burden which Habakkuk tha prophet did see.
O LORD, how long shall I cry, N u will not hear! even cry out 2 u of violence, N u will not save!
Why do u show me iniquity, N cause me 2 look grievance? 4 spoiling N violence r before me: N there r dat raise up strife N contention.
Therefore tha law is slacked, N judgment does never go forth: 4 tha wicked does compass about tha righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceeds.
Look y’all among tha heathen, N regard, N wonder marvellously: 4 I will work a work in ur days, which y’all will not believe, though it be told u.
4, look, I raise up tha Chaldeans, dat bitter N hasty nation, which shall march through tha breadth of tha land, 2 possess tha dwellingplaces dat r not theirs.
Dey r terrible N dreadful: their judgment N their dignity shall proceed of themselves.

Their horses also r swifter than tha leopards, N r more fierce than tha evening wolves: N their horsemen shall spread themselves, N their horsemen shall come from far; dey shall fly as tha eagle dat hurries 2 eat.
Dey shall come all 4 violence: their faces shall sup up as tha east wind, N dey shall gather tha captivity as tha sand.
N dey shall scoff at tha kings, N tha princes shall be a scorn 2 ’em: dey shall deride every strong hold; 4 dey shall heap dust, N take it.
Then shall his mind change, N he shall pass over, N offend, imputing dis his power 2 his god.
R u not from everlasting, O LORD my God, mine Holy One? we shall not die. O LORD, u have ordained ’em 4 judgment; N, O mighty God, u have established ’em 4 correction.
u r of purer eyes than 2 look evil, N can not look on iniquity: so look u upon ’em dat deal treacherously, N hold ur tongue when tha wicked devours tha man dat is more righteous than he?
N make men as tha fishes of tha sea, as tha creeping things, dat have no ruler over ’em?
Dey take up all of ’em wit tha angle, dey catch ’em in their net, N gather ’em in their drag: therefore dey rejoice N r glad.
Therefore dey sacrifice 2 their net, N burn incense 2 their drag; because by ’em their portion is fat, N their food plenteous.
Shall dey therefore empty their net, N not spare continually 2 kill tha nations?

2.text: I will stand upon my watch, N set me upon tha tower, N will watch 2 see what he will say 2 me, N what I shall answer when I am reproved.
N tha LORD answered me, N said, Write tha vision, N make it plain upon tables, dat he may run dat readeth it.
4 tha vision is yet 4 an appointed time, but at tha end it shall speak, N not lie: though it tarry, wait 4 it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.
Look, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him: but tha just shall live by his faith.

Yeah also, because he transgresseth by wine, he is a proud man, neither keeps at home, who enlargeth his desire as hell, N is as death, N cannot be satisfied, but gathers 2 him all nations, N heapeth 2 him all people:
Shall not all dese take up a parable against him, N a taunting proverb against him, N say, woe 2 him dat increases dat which is not his! how long? N 2 him dat ladeth himself wit thick clay!
Shall dey not rise up suddenly dat shall bite u, N awake dat shall vex u, N u will be 4 booties 2 ’em?
Because u have spoiled many nations, all tha remnant of tha people shall spoil u; because of men’s blood, N 4 tha violence of tha land, of tha city, N of all dat live in it.
Woe 2 him dat coveteth an evil covetousness 2 his house, dat he may set his nest on high, dat he may be delivered from tha power of evil!
u have consulted shame 2 ur house by cuttin off many people, N have sinned against ur soul.
4 tha stone shall cry out of tha wall, N tha beam out of tha timber shall answer it.
Woe 2 him dat builds a town wit blood, N stablisheth a city by iniquity!
Look, is it not of tha LORD of hosts dat tha people shall labour in tha very fire, N tha people shall weary themselves 4 very vanity?
4 tha earth shall be filled wit tha knowledge of tha glory of tha LORD, as tha waterz cover tha sea.
Woe 2 him dat gives his neighbour drink, dat put ur bottle 2 him, N make him drunken also, dat u may look on their nakedness!
u r filled wit shame 4 glory: drink u also, N let ur foreskin be uncovered: tha cup of tha LORD’s right hand shall be turned 2 u, N shameful spewing shall be on ur glory.
4 tha violence of Lebanon shall cover u, N tha spoil of beasts, which made ’em afraid, because of men’s blood, N 4 tha violence of tha land, of tha city, N of all dat live in it.
What profits tha graven image dat tha maker of it has graven it; tha molten image, N a teacher of lies, dat tha maker of his work trusts in it, 2 make dumb idols?
Woe 2 him dat says 2 tha wood, Awake; 2 tha dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach! look, it is laid over wit gold N silver, N there is no breath at all in tha midst of it.
But tha LORD is in his holy temple: let all tha earth keep silence before him.

3.text: A prayer of Habakkuk tha prophet upon Shigionoth.
O LORD, I have heard ur speech, N was afraid: O LORD, revive ur work in tha midst of tha years, in tha midst of tha years make known; in wrath remember mercy.
God came from Teman, N tha Holy One from mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered tha heavenz, N tha earth was full of his praise.
N his brightness was as tha light; he had horns comin out of his hand: N there was tha hidin of his power.
Before him went tha pestilence, N burnin coals went forth at his feet.
He stood, N measured tha earth: he beheld, N drove asunder tha nations; N tha everlasting mountains were scattered, tha perpetual hills did bow: his ways r everlasting.
I saw tha tents of Cushan in affliction: N tha curtains of tha land of Midian did tremble.
Was tha LORD displeased against tha rivers? was thine anger against tha rivers? was ur wrath against tha sea, dat u did ride upon thine horses N ur chariots of salvation?
Ur bow was made quite naked, according 2 tha oaths of tha tribes, even ur word. Selah. u did cleave tha earth wit rivers.
Tha mountains saw u, N dey trembled: tha overflowing of tha water passed by: tha deep uttered his voice, N lifted up his hands on high.
Tha sun N moon stood still in their habitation: at tha light of thine arrows dey went, N at tha shinin of ur glittering spear.
u did march through tha land in indignation, u did thresh tha heathen in anger.
u went forth 4 tha salvation of ur people, even 4 salvation wit thine anointed; u woundedst tha head out of tha house of tha wicked, by discovering tha foundation 2 tha neck. Selah.
u did strike through wit his staves tha head of his villages: dey came out as a whirlwind 2 scatter me: their rejoicin was as 2 devour tha poor secretly.
u did walk through tha sea wit thine horses, through tha heap of great waterz.

When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at tha voice: rottenness entered in2 my bones, N I trembled in myself, dat I might rest in tha day of trouble: when he comes up 2 tha people, he will invade ’em wit his troops.

Although tha fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in tha vines; tha labour of tha olive shall fail, N tha fields shall yield no food; tha flock shall be cut off from tha fold, N there shall be no herd in tha stalls:
Yet I will rejoice in tha LORD, I will joy in tha God of my salvation.
Tha LORD God is my strength, N he will make my feet like hinds’ feet, N he will make me 2 walk upon mine high places. 2 tha chief singer on my stringed instruments.
